blocks.heading: Questionnaires and seasonal effects
blocks.text:
A tourism questionnaire can investigate visitors' activities or residents' experiences, but its target population must be stated. A visitor survey cannot represent residents merely because it asks about the destination. Use clear, neutral questions, suitable answer options and an opportunity to decline. Avoid collecting names or unnecessary personal information. Pilot the questions to identify ambiguity before starting the main sample.

![Resident questionnaire sheet with consent, neutral question and tally](../../assets/images/ITEM-6137-2.3-040-PROC-answer.png)

blocks.text: Random selection uses a chance rule within a defined group; systematic selection follows a rule such as every fifth person passing; stratified selection makes sure groups such as residents, visitors and business owners are all included. Record people who decline instead of replacing them silently with convenient respondents.

Closed questions offer fixed answers, such as yes/no, tick boxes or a 1–5 rating scale; they are quick to answer and easy to tally and graph. Open questions, such as “Why did you visit?”, give detail but are harder to group. Keep wording short and neutral: “Has tourism changed your household income?”, not “Tourism has helped you, hasn't it?”. A pilot survey with a few people shows which questions confuse. Remembered answers about a past season are perceptions, not direct counts.

Business surveys judge tourism's economic and seasonal impact. Ask owners or managers of lodges, shops, craft stalls and tour operators which months are busiest, whether they employ extra staff in the busy season, roughly what share of customers are tourists, and where most supplies are bought: locally, elsewhere in Namibia or imported. Busy and quiet season answers show changes in income and jobs; the supplies question shows leakage.

State the sample size with every result: twelve “yes” answers from 20 residents is 60% of that sample, not of all residents. Use a pie chart or divided bar for shares in each category, and side-by-side bars to compare a quiet and a busy season.
